scores.critique: Cloth spec is the most correct of the three (baked SDF grid with analytic trilinear gradient, smin joints, 10 substeps x 1 GS iteration with lambda reset, rest-length seam ramp, Macklin-2014 friction formula written correctly, gravity ramp + 5x damping in sew phase, 5 m/s clamp = 8.3 mm/substep < thinnest limb). Bergou/Wardetzky K-vector and coef=3/(2(A0+A1)) match Bender's PBD formulation, and the sign self-test in risk #6 is the right guard. But: (1) boundary-repair midpoint insertion on a seam edge silently breaks the 'both sides have n+1 vertices' invariant - nothing inserts the matching point on the partner edge; (2) an unjittered regular hex lattice is exactly co-circular, which is the worst input for naive Bowyer-Watson in floats - expect sliver/inconsistent triangulations; (3) bend-compliance table is dynamically flat: with w~3e4, coef~7.5e3/m^2 and h_sub=1/600, Sum w|grad C|^2 is ~1e7-1e8 while alpha~=alpha*3.6e5 is 1.8e6 (cotton) to 1e8 (chiffon), so cotton and leather will bend almost identically until retuned (setStiffnessScale helps but the table is mislabelled as tuned); (4) MarchingCubes at 128^3 over a 2 m cube is a 15.6 mm voxel - the body will be blobby with a 2M-cell field to fill on every bake, and the primitives-only fallback looks like a capsule man; (5) the measure->rescale->rebake feedback loop on breast/buttock blending is extra work with oscillation risk for a cosmetic readout; (6) units are mixed inside one document (body.params cm except height m and 0..1 blends; sizes.rows mm) - guaranteed 'Fit body to size' bug; (7) the T-shirt sample says '6 seams' and lists 8; (8) Tab as pane-swap fights browser focus; (9) ~25 primitives with smin at 580k cells is 150-300 ms on a good machine, probably more on the target laptop, and the 30 mm drag-grid means collisions jump on pointer-up; (10) Phase 0 '1 h' for types+store+events+fabrics+two hand-authored garments+index.html ids is not credible. Ownership is clean (geometry outside core/, samples in their own dir, popout excluded from automated acceptance), which is why the agent-conflict surface is the lowest of the three despite the most moving parts.

Best pattern-making semantics (per-edge allowance with hem square-off, cutOnFold/fold edge, notches keep t under grading, ease % readout, closed-form Ramanujan radius which is actually correct since P is linear in a at fixed aspect). Physics is the weakest: (1) 'stretch compliance scaled by 1/edgeLength' is inverted - for membrane-like behaviour alpha must scale with L (alpha = L/K), 1/L makes short edges softer; (2) collision is a per-particle loop over ~17 analytic primitives (not '6') with pow() superellipse evaluation and finite-difference normals (4-7 SDF evals per particle per substep) - the '<2 ms at 6k particles x 8 substeps' claim is off by roughly 5x, and plain min-union gives gradient discontinuities at armpit/crotch that cause jitter; (3) no self-collision in v1 means the collar/hem front-back interpenetrate on the very first demo, which is the 'SIGGRAPH-style' selling point; (4) 5 cm per-substep displacement clamp is larger than a forearm diameter (only the 4 m/s clamp saves it); (5) after L=0 seams are 'welded by averaging masses/positions each substep' - a second code path duplicating what the rigid constraint already does. Sloan edge-recovery via flips is 100+ tricky lines for one agent, though the ear-clip fallback is sound. Segment stores p0 AND p1 with a 'shared endpoint' invariant - every editor tool must update two records. Lead writes samples into src/pattern/ which agent P owns (ownership overlap). Acceptance #12 calls __app.ui.popout() which is window.open without user activation - Chromium blocks it unless launched with --disable-popup-blocking; #5 measures chest 'within 0.5%' from the same loft that was solved (tautological) or from a 32-gon (already 0.16% low). Per-point grade deltas, 'dress' sample, anisotropy hooks, stress heat-map and grade nests are scope creep for one session.

Most product-shaped spec: drape() on load, __app.ready, sim.step(n) returns stats, ui.click(id), page-count formula in acceptance, seam-neighbour self-collision mask, debounced SDF re-bake with grid swap, snapshot restore on NaN, and the only candidate whose midpoint insertion also inserts on the partner chain (preserving seam parity, with a correct Gabriel-condition argument). Fewest exotic algorithms (distance bending, grid SDF, mergeGeometries body). Errors: (1) fabric table is 2-3 orders of magnitude too stiff - stretch 2e-6 and bend 4e-4 m/N give alpha~ of 0.26 and 52 against Sum w|grad C|^2 ~ 6e4, so every constraint is rigid and cotton/silk/chiffon drape identically; (2) pattern space is y-down while outlines are 'CCW' and offset uses 'right-hand normal of CCW = outward' - the orientation conventions flip in a y-down frame; (3) multi-edge seam chains with 'interior corners forced as samples' do not yield equal sample counts on both sides as claimed (chain A with a corner gets an extra point); (4) 6 substeps with vMax 8 m/s permits 22 mm per substep against ~25 mm wrist/forearm radius and 4 mm offset - the sign-flip check mitigates but is not a guarantee; (5) Laplacian smoothing after Delaunay can degrade boundary-adjacent triangles and is unnecessary once the lattice is jittered; (6) bisection on Ramanujan '5 iterations <0.1%' is wrong (1/32 of bracket) and unnecessary since the closed form exists; (7) acceptance #13 clicks the canvas at 'known mm->px coordinates' but __app exposes no view transform; #12 needs popups allowed; (8) A1 owns core/geometry.js inside A0's frozen core/, and A8 owns fabric/ + ui/ + all panels + styles - overloaded; 10 agents including A0/A9 is at the top of the budget; (9) quantity:2 + flip instancing with pieceInstanceId keys adds indexing complexity to mesher, physics, render and export simultaneously; (10) central-difference gradient (7 trilinear samples) where the analytic trilinear gradient is free.

grafts: product-first: add __app.ready (resolves after first mesh+body+drape) and make sim.step(n) run n frames synchronously (render suppressed) and return the stats object - the backbone of every acceptance check.
product-first: drape() = arrange + sew + play as the default action on load and on loadSample; the app must show a draped T-shirt within 5 s with no clicks.

product-first: when boundary repair inserts a midpoint on a seam edge, insert the matching point on the partner edge at the same arc-length fraction so seam vertex counts stay equal (fixes physics-first's parity bug); keep its Gabriel-condition reasoning (interior clearance >= 0.6h, boundary segments <= h) as the documented justification.
product-first: seam-neighbour self-collision mask - skip vertex pairs within 2 rings of a seam pair so sewing is never fought by self-collision.

product-first: SDF re-bake is debounced (~150 ms) and the solver keeps colliding with the old grid until the new Float32Array is swapped in atomically; plus the 'if sign(d) flips between xPrev and x, project to xPrev's side' tunnelling check.

product-first: body render mesh = torso loft (32 segments x 1 ring/cm) + capsule/round-cone/ellipsoid limbs merged with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries into one indexed geometry - use this instead of the MarchingCubes addon as the v1 body visual (MC becomes v2).

product-first: '_cm' / '_mm' suffixes on every measurement key so the doc is self-describing; adaptive substeps (drop 10->6 with a status-bar 'reduced quality' flag when msStep > 20 for 30 frames); periodic sane-state snapshot restored on NaN instead of a full reset; tiled-print acceptance = ceil(W/190)*ceil(H/277) page count; ui.click(id).

patternmaking-first: jitter the interior lattice by a seeded deterministic +-0.15h (retry with a new seed up to 3x) and gate mesh quality on min angle > 20 deg for 98% of triangles - removes the co-circular hex-lattice failure mode in Bowyer-Watson.
patternmaking-first: closed-form ellipse semi-axis from circumference via Ramanujan (a = P / (pi[3(1+k) - sqrt((3+k)(1+3k))]) at fixed aspect k) - no bisection, no rebake correction pass.
patternmaking-first: after arrangement, sample the SDF for every particle and push any d<0 particle out along the normal before the first step.

patternmaking-first: seam ease % readout ('A 312 mm / B 328 mm - ease 5.1%') in the status bar and seam list; per-size ease-drift check (>3% from base) in the Sizes panel; notches keep parameter t under grading.

patternmaking-first: cutOnFold semantics for export - print the half piece with 'PLACE ON FOLD' label and dash-dot fold edge (physics-first already mirrors at mesh time but exports nothing about the fold).

patternmaking-first: per-module selftest.js exporting runSelfTest() callable from __app, so each agent has a green/red gate before integration; calibration square on every printed tile, not only page 1.
patternmaking-first (v1.5 only, reserve schema field now): per-edge seam allowance with hem square-off rule, and grade nests (all sizes of one piece in one SVG).
corrections: physics-first remesh: inserting a midpoint into a seam edge during boundary repair without inserting on the partner edge breaks the equal-vertex-count seam invariant - insert on both sides at the same fraction, or resample both sides with n+1.

physics-first remesh: an unjittered hex lattice is exactly co-circular; naive Bowyer-Watson in floating point on it produces inconsistent/sliver triangulations. Jitter deterministically (+-0.05..0.15h).

Fabric compliance tables in all three are unvalidated numbers: with a 15 mm mesh, w ~ 3e4 1/kg and h_sub = 1/600..1/360, product-first's stretch 2e-6 and bend 4e-4 m/N make every constraint rigid (alpha~ 0.26 / 52 vs Sum w|grad C|^2 ~ 6e4), and physics-first's Bergou bend values (5..300) are all in the 'nearly rigid' regime (alpha~ 1.8e6..1e8 vs ~1e8). The spec must state the intended ratio r = alpha~ / Sum w|grad C|^2 per fabric (e.g. cotton bend ~0.3, silk ~5, chiffon ~20), derive the table from it, expose a global stiffness scale, and make 'silk sags visibly more than denim on the hanging-sheet fixture' an acceptance check.

patternmaking-first: 'stretch compliance scaled by 1/edgeLength' is inverted. For membrane behaviour a distance constraint's compliance must scale with rest length: alpha_edge = L / K_membrane (alpha proportional to L).

patternmaking-first: per-particle analytic SDF over ~17 primitives with pow()-based superellipse and finite-difference normals costs 4-7 evaluations per particle per substep - not '<2 ms'. Bake to a uniform grid (physics-first 15 mm / product-first 10 mm) and use the analytic trilinear gradient, not central differences (product-first's 7-sample gradient is wasted work).

Plain min-union of primitives leaves gradient discontinuities at armpit/crotch that make cloth jitter; use polynomial smooth-min (k ~ 0.04 m) at joints when baking (physics-first does; patternmaking-first and product-first do not).

product-first pattern space: y-down + 'CCW outline' + 'right-hand normal is outward' is self-contradictory across a frame flip. Use y-up mm in the document (flip once in SVG export, as physics-first/patternmaking-first do) and define 'outward' from the signed-area sign of the stored polygon, never from a named winding.

product-first seams: multi-edge chains with 'interior corners forced as samples' do not guarantee equal counts on both sides. v1 seams span single edges (split tool first, as physics-first/patternmaking-first specify); if chains are kept, both sides must be sampled with the same n by chain-fraction and corners snapped to the nearest sample.

product-first: 6 substeps with an 8 m/s clamp is 22 mm/substep - larger than the 4 mm collision offset and comparable to wrist/forearm radius. Use >= 8-10 substeps, clamp <= 5 m/s and a per-substep displacement clamp <= 0.5 * mesh spacing.

product-first: drop Laplacian smoothing after Delaunay (can invert/degrade boundary triangles; jitter makes it unnecessary) and replace 5-iteration bisection on Ramanujan with the closed form (P is linear in a at fixed aspect).

physics-first body: MarchingCubes at 128^3 over a 2 m cube is a 15.6 mm voxel (blobby body, 2M field cells per bake) and the addon's geometry/isolation conventions are a known time sink; render the merged loft+capsule mesh instead. Also make the measure->rescale->rebake correction pass report-only in v1 (feedback loop for a cosmetic readout).

physics-first units: body.params mixes cm, m (height) and 0..1 blends while sizes.rows are mm. Pick one unit per family with suffixed keys (chest_cm, height_cm; size rows in the same unit) and convert only in units.js.

physics-first sample garment: the T-shirt is listed as '6 seams' but enumerates 8 (2 shoulder, 2 side, 2 sleeve cap, 2 underarm); the lead must run the mesher over the hand-authored samples before fan-out and assert seam partner lengths within 3%.

Automated acceptance must not depend on window.open from a script: Chromium blocks popups without user activation. Either exclude the pop-out from the automated suite (physics-first) or document launching Chromium with --disable-popup-blocking; same for product-first's about:blank + document.write export window (return the HTML string, and let tests parse it).

product-first acceptance #13 (clicking the canvas at 'known mm->px coordinates') is not automatable as written - __app must expose pattern.worldToScreen(x,y)/setView(pan,zoom) or the test must use __app.pattern.addSeam.

Measurement acceptance ('chest within 0.5%/1 cm') is tautological when measured from the analytic loft that was solved from the same number; measure from the baked SDF or the union mesh (physics-first's ray-bisection does this) and set the tolerance accordingly (1.5 cm is realistic once breasts/shoulder spheres blend in).

Ownership: keep geometry, samples and popout out of the frozen core/ (product-first has A1 writing core/geometry.js; patternmaking-first has the lead writing into agent P's src/pattern/samples). Every Phase-0 file must live in a directory no Phase-1 agent owns.

Phase 0 is not '~1 h': all typedefs, store with undo, event names, index.html ids, two hand-authored garments validated by a mesher, and throwing stubs is 2-3 h of lead time; budget it, and have the cloth agent start against its own sphere-SDF fixture (physics-first's cloth/testfields.js) so it never blocks on the body agent.
Avoid Tab as a shortcut (physics-first pane swap, patternmaking-first measure tool) - it collides with browser focus navigation and confuses automation.
